answer: A trusted trades list is a short, vetted bench of painters, flooring installers, door and window installers, masons and general renovators that an agent can suggest to sellers before listing. With more listings and pickier buyers, it helps sellers get pre-listing work moving, as long as agents vet each trade, disclose referral relationships and let sellers choose.

blocks.x: A market that rewards preparation

The [Winnipeg Regional Real Estate Board](https://www.winnipegregionalrealestatenews.com/market-statistics/market-releases/article/629/more-choice-record-average-prices-and-softer-sales-defined-september-results) reported September 2026 sales down about 10% and listings up about 14%, with detached-home listings up about 20%. The year-to-date detached average is a record, but buyers have more options. That raises the value of a trusted trades list for real estate agents.

The Bank of Canada's [October 2026 rate hike](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/10/fad-press-release-2026-10-28/) adds pressure. Buyers with tighter budgets may be less willing to take on homes that need work.
In this market, homes that look move-in ready have an edge. The question for sellers is who will get the work done, and how quickly.
Sellers want one call, not ten

Many sellers do not have a contractor list. They are often busy, sometimes relocating, and sometimes selling an estate. When an agent recommends [pre-listing work](/blog/pre-listing-renovations-winnipeg) such as painting, a few repairs and new flooring, the seller's next question is: "Who can do that?"
Agents who can answer with confidence gain trust. Agents who say "try searching online" leave sellers to manage a stressful process on their own, which can delay the listing.
Getting a written quote from a trusted contractor, with a clear scope and timeline, lets the seller weigh the cost against the likely effect on price and time on market.
Our view: the agent is the project quarterback

The best agents act as coordinators for pre-listing work. They do not do the work, and they should not take responsibility for it, but they connect sellers with trusted trades and keep the timeline moving.
A strong bench includes:

blocks.x: What to look for in painters
Painting is a common pre-listing job. It makes rooms look cleaner and more neutral in photos, and it covers marks and wear.
But results depend on the crew. Professional painters in Winnipeg should bring:
**Proper preparation:** patching, sanding, priming.
**Clean lines** that look sharp in photos.
**Reliability,** showing up as promised so photos and listing dates hold.
A poor paint job can do more harm than good, because buyers notice drips, patchy coverage and paint on trim.

On older homes, ask how the crew plans around lead paint. [Health Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/home-safety/lead-based-paint.html) says a house built before 1960 probably has lead-based paint, and warns against using sanders or heat guns to remove it.
Building and maintaining your trusted trades list

**Vet trades properly:** run [WCB's clearance search](/blog/how-to-check-a-contractors-wcb-clearance-manitoba), check the Companies Office, look up past job addresses in the City's permit search, confirm insurance and ask for references.
**Start small:** try a new trade on a simple job before recommending them widely.
**Get feedback** from clients after every job.
**Disclose relationships** with any trades you refer, in line with your brokerage's rules.
**Let sellers choose:** recommend more than one option where possible, and make it clear the contract is between the seller and the trade.
Timing for spring

Spring is usually a busy listing season, and trades can book up early. Agents with spring listings should line up painting and repairs now. Interior painting can be done over the winter; exterior painting and masonry need to wait for warmer weather, so book those early for the first suitable weeks, usually in late spring.
The bottom line

In a market with more listings and choosier buyers, preparation helps sell homes. Agents who maintain a vetted bench of trades can help sellers move from "thinking about it" to "listed", and help their listings stand out when buyers have plenty to compare.
